event: Elsie wakes in the hay with Cora's hand still in hers, and Cora asleep, her bun come loose.

pictured.coverAfter: Elsie woke to grey light in the little square window and the smell
pictured.outfit: charcoal coat, bun come loose, hair half down

event: Elsie lies still and looks at Cora's sleeping face, all its guard gone.
Cora wakes, sees their hands, and takes hers back as if from a stove.
Cora is down the ladder pinning up her hair before anyone else stirs.
Tamsin wakes with hay in her curls; Tilly wakes with hay everywhere.
At the well Elsie tells everyone cheerfully that Cora held her hand all night, and it was cold.

event: Tamsin drops the bucket; Tilly goes very still; Cora turns scarlet to the collar.
Elsie says she'll knit Cora gloves, and wonders why everyone has gone so quiet.
The headwoman brings porridge, and says the trolls fished all night and took no sheep.

event: Down at the bridge the young troll waves to Tilly from the pool; the mother only watches.
They start back south along the Wend in the morning sun.
Tamsin walks close to Elsie and says, low, that she'd hold Elsie's hand too, if it's cold.
Elsie gives her hand at once, and Tamsin holds it all the way to the next stile.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 60 → 62 (confidence: asks to hold Elsie's hand, and is given it)

event: Elsie takes out her notebook and asks Tilly more favourite things, to fill out Tilly's page.
Tilly lists pear fizz, blue flames and the smell of sulphur, then goes red and stops.
Elsie asks what the last one was; Tilly says it's a secret and walks faster.
Elsie asks Cora hers; Cora says tea, black, one sugar, as Elsie already knows.
Elsie waits, and Cora adds, very quietly: and lavender.
They come in through the north gate, and the gate clerk logs them in with a grin.
At the guild hall the talk stops when they walk in, then starts up again louder.
Two adventurers at the board say troll, and bargain, and Enthraller, and one raises his mug.
A clerk meets them at the door: the guildmaster wants Elsie and Cora upstairs now.
Tamsin and Tilly wait by the board while Elsie and Cora go up.
The guildmaster has heard of the toll bridge already, and waves them to chairs.
She asks Elsie to tell her plainly what happened at the toll bridge.
Elsie tells her: the hunger, the silted pools, the weir, the trout.
The guildmaster asks why she didn't let the Berserker kill them asleep.
Elsie says she wanted to ask the trolls what they needed first.
The guildmaster looks at Cora; Cora reads her ledger aloud and says that is exactly what she saw.
The guildmaster asks Elsie what she wants from the guild.
Elsie says a blue-doored house on Willow Canal, for all her friends, and the guildmaster laughs.
The guildmaster says that's more than most adventurers ask for, and less than they should.
She says the city is talking, not all kindly: an Enthraller who talks to trolls frightens some more.
Elsie asks why; the guildmaster says, because it works.
She tells Cora to go on writing every line, and sends them down.
On the stairs Cora says it's the first time she has heard the guildmaster laugh.
Downstairs Tamsin and Tilly pounce on them for news.
Elsie says the guildmaster laughed about the house, and Tamsin says that's a good sign.
On the E-rank board are wolves on the north road, Bellmoor barrow, and bandits at Hollin Ford.
Tilly says bandits pay best; Tamsin says bandits fight back.
Elsie asks about the barrow; Tamsin reads that there are lights and singing there at night.
Elsie says she'd like to know who's singing, and they take the barrow for tomorrow.
The clerk enters the party for Bellmoor barrow, and Cora writes it in her ledger.
Cora says she has her report to write, and goes to the charcoal door.
At the Tipsy Heron Tamsin pays for stew and bread for the three of them.
A tall woman with her arm in a sling sits at the next table: the Hounds' shield-bearer.
Tamsin sees her, goes white, and puts down her spoon.
Elsie feels it down the Tether, shame like cold water, and puts a hand on Tamsin's knee.
Tamsin gets up, walks to the shield-bearer's table, and stands there.
She says she's sorry about the arm, and should have said so a week ago.
The shield-bearer looks at her a long time, then says she heard about the wolves and the Tether.
She says it was the red, not Tamsin, and she knows the difference now, and holds out her good hand.
Tamsin shakes it, and comes back to the table blinking hard.
Elsie hugs her round the middle, and Tilly hugs them both.
They walk to Willow Canal; the card is still in the blue-doored house's window.
Elsie works out on her fingers what they've saved against what the agent wants, and sighs.
Tamsin says the barrow pays ten lanterns; Tilly says that's still a great many barrows.
Elsie kisses two fingers and presses them to the blue door.
Tilly goes home to brew for the barrow, hugging Elsie twice.
Tamsin walks Elsie home, saying she'll write to Nell about the shield-bearer tonight.
At the Honeycomb door Tamsin hugs her and goes off toward the wharf office.
In the attic Elsie writes Tilly's favourite things, leaving a gap for the secret one.
Under Cora, below tea, bun and quiet, she adds: black, one sugar; lavender.
Downstairs she asks the baker where to buy wool, and the baker says Spindle Lane.
On Spindle Lane Elsie buys grey wool, the grey of Cora's eyes, and pays for it.
She buys knitting needles too, and pays for those.
At the round window she casts on the first glove, humming.
Moonpenny sits beside her on the sill, closed up for the day.
The lamplighters' boats come by at dusk, and Elsie has a cuff done.
She sees Cora walking alone along Thimble Canal again, and waves.
Cora looks up and lifts her hand at once this time.
Elsie holds up the grey cuff on its needles; Cora tilts her head, puzzled, and walks on.
Elsie writes her mother about the guildmaster laughing, the house, and the gloves.
Down the Tether Tamsin's shame is gone, eased like a knot let out.
